filing_civil_lawsuit.title: Filing a Civil Lawsuit
steps: File Plaint at the Relevant Court
District Court (if the claim exceeds LKR 1.5M)
Magistrate’s Court (if the claim is less than or equal to LKR 1.5M)
Pay Court Fees (based on claim amount, as per the court's fee structure)
Court Issues Summons to Defendant (Defendant has 14 days to respond)
Does the Defendant File an Answer?
Yes → Proceed to Pre-Trial
No → Default Judgment Issued
Pre-Trial & Mediation (Attempt at settlement or alternative dispute resolution)
Settlement? → Case Closed
No Settlement → Proceed to Trial
Trial & Evidence Review (Plaintiff and Defendant present their arguments, witnesses, and evidence)
Court Issues Judgment
Favorable to Plaintiff? → Go to Enforcement
Favorable to Defendant? → Case Dismissed / Appeal Option
Enforcement of Judgment (Execution of the court's decision, like garnishment, asset seizure, etc.)
End

Court Issues Judgment

Favorable to Defendant? → Case Dismissed / Appeal Option

End

divorce_procedure.title: Step-by-Step Divorce Procedure in Sri Lanka
steps: Understanding Grounds for Divorce (Adultery, Malicious Desertion, Incurable Impotency.  Mutual consent is not a valid reason.)
Hiring a Lawyer (Assess divorce grounds, gather evidence, discuss legal fees.) [Uncontested: LKR 75,000 to 150,000 | Contested: LKR 150,000 to 500,000+]
Filing for Divorce in the District Court (File Plaint, pay court stamp fee, receive case number and hearing date.) [Filing Fees: LKR 3,000 to 10,000 | Stamp Duty: LKR 1,000 to 5,000]
Serving Summons to the Respondent (Summons issued; if the respondent doesnt appear, court may proceed ex-parte.) [Summons Cost: LKR 1,500 to 5,000]
Mediation and Reconciliation Attempts (Court may refer to mediation; if reconciliation fails, the case proceeds.) [Mediation: Usually free]
Trial Proceedings (If Mediation Fails) (Petitioner presents evidence; respondent can defend.) [Legal Fees: LKR 250,000 to 1,000,000+]
Courts Decision (Issuing Decree Nisi) (If evidence is sufficient, Decree Nisi is issued; 3-month waiting period applies.  Appeal possible.) [Court Costs: LKR 5,000 to 15,000]
Issuing the Final Divorce Order (Decree Absolute) (After 3 months, court issues Decree Absolute, legally ending the marriage.) [Final Divorce Certificate: LKR 1,500 to 3,000]

Settling Related Matters (Child Custody: Determined by court [LKR 50,000 to 200,000] | Property Division: Based on contributions [LKR 100,000 to 500,000+] | Alimony: Ordered if spouse is financially dependent.)

animal_attack_procedure.title: Step-by-Step Procedure for Animal Attack Cases in Sri Lanka
steps: Seeking Immediate Medical Attention (Visit the nearest hospital, obtain medical records, and report the injury to the doctor.) [Hospital Fees: LKR 2,000 to 25,000 depending on severity]
Reporting the Incident to Police (File a complaint at the local police station, provide details of the attack, and obtain a police report.) [Police Report: Free]
Identifying the Responsible Party (If the animal has an owner, they may be held liable. If it's a stray, municipal authorities may be responsible.)
Consulting a Lawyer (Discuss legal options, gather evidence such as medical reports, witness statements, and photos.) [Legal Consultation Fees: LKR 5,000 to 25,000]
Filing a Case in the District Court (Initiate a civil lawsuit against the responsible party for compensation.) [Filing Fees: LKR 3,000 to 10,000 | Court Stamp Duty: LKR 1,000 to 5,000]
Summoning the Defendant (Court issues summons to the responsible party to appear in court.) [Summons Cost: LKR 1,500 to 5,000]
Mediation or Out-of-Court Settlement (Parties may opt for mediation to reach a settlement without proceeding to trial.) [Mediation: Free or LKR 5,000 to 15,000 if private]
Trial Proceedings (If no settlement is reached, the case proceeds to trial where both parties present evidence.) [Legal Fees: LKR 50,000 to 300,000+ depending on complexity]
Court Decision and Compensation (If the court rules in favor of the victim, compensation is awarded based on medical costs, lost wages, and suffering.) [Court Costs: LKR 5,000 to 15,000]
Appeal Process (If either party is dissatisfied with the judgment, they may appeal to the Provincial High Court.) [Appeal Fees: LKR 10,000 to 50,000]
Final Settlement and Compensation Payment (Once the verdict is finalized, the liable party must pay compensation as ordered by the court.)

wrongful_birth_procedure.title: Step-by-Step Procedure for Wrongful Birth or Wrongful Life Claims in Sri Lanka
steps: Understanding the Legal Basis (Wrongful birth and wrongful life cases fall under medical negligence law. Parents can sue a doctor or hospital if they failed to detect or disclose a congenital disability that could have led to a different medical decision.)

Hiring a Medical Negligence Lawyer (Consult a lawyer specializing in medical malpractice to assess the case and review medical records.) [Consultation Fees: LKR 10,000 to 50,000 | Case Preparation Fees: LKR 50,000 to 200,000]
Gathering Evidence (Collect all medical records, expert medical opinions, and witness testimonies to prove negligence.) [Medical Reports & Expert Opinions: LKR 5,000 to 20,000]

Filing a Case in the District Court (File a lawsuit in the District Court where the negligence occurred, with a plaint detailing the medical malpractice and damages sought.) [Filing Fees: LKR 3,000 to 10,000 | Stamp Duty: LKR 1,000 to 5,000]
Serving Summons to the Defendant (Summons is issued to the doctor or hospital, requiring them to respond. If they fail to appear, the court may proceed ex-parte.) [Summons Cost: LKR 1,500 to 5,000]

Mediation and Settlement Discussions (The court may encourage mediation between the parties to reach a settlement before trial.) [Court-Supervised Mediation: Free | Private Mediation: LKR 5,000 to 15,000]

Trial Proceedings at the District Court (If mediation fails, the case goes to trial. Both sides present arguments, medical expert testimonies, and evidence.) [Legal Fees for Trial: LKR 100,000 to 500,000+]

Courts Decision and Awarding of Compensation (If the court finds the doctor/hospital guilty of negligence, compensation is awarded for medical expenses, emotional distress, and future costs of care.) [Court Costs: LKR 5,000 to 15,000]
Appeal Process (If either party is dissatisfied with the ruling, they can file an appeal at the Provincial High Court within 30 days.) [Appeal Fees: LKR 10,000 to 50,000]
Final Settlement and Compensation Payment (If the ruling is in favor of the plaintiff, the hospital/doctor must pay the awarded compensation. If they fail, legal enforcement measures can be taken.)

land_dispute_procedure.title: Step-by-Step Land Dispute Resolution in Sri Lanka
steps: Understanding the Nature of the Dispute (Determine if the issue is ownership, boundary conflict, or encroachment. Gather necessary documents like title deeds and survey plans.)
Hiring a Land Lawyer (Consult a property law specialist to assess legal options and documentation.) [Consultation Fees: LKR 10,000 to 50,000 | Case Preparation: LKR 50,000 to 200,000]

Obtaining Land Documents and Surveys (Collect essential documents such as title deeds, land registry extracts, and an updated survey plan from a licensed surveyor.) [Certified Copies: LKR 2,000 to 5,000 | Survey Plan: LKR 10,000 to 50,000 | Land Registry Extracts: LKR 1,000 to 3,000]
Sending a Legal Notice (A lawyer issues a notice to the opposing party requesting a resolution before litigation.) [Legal Notice Cost: LKR 5,000 to 15,000]

Filing a Case in the District Court (If no resolution is reached, a lawsuit is filed at the relevant District Court where the land is located.) [Filing Fees: LKR 3,000 to 10,000 | Stamp Duty: LKR 1,000 to 5,000]
Serving Summons to the Defendant (Court issues summons to notify the opposing party of the legal action.) [Summons Cost: LKR 1,500 to 5,000]
Court-Ordered Mediation (Optional) (The court may suggest mediation to resolve the dispute before trial.) [Court Mediation: Free | Private Mediation: LKR 5,000 to 15,000]

Trial Proceedings in the District Court (If mediation fails, the case proceeds to trial where both parties present evidence, witnesses, and legal arguments.) [Legal Fees: LKR 100,000 to 500,000+ | Court Costs: LKR 5,000 to 15,000]
Court Decision and Judgment (The court rules on the ownership, boundaries, or encroachment claims. The losing party may be required to vacate or compensate the rightful owner.)

Appeal Process (If Necessary) (If dissatisfied, a party can appeal the District Courts ruling to the Civil Appellate High Court and, in rare cases, the Supreme Court.) [Appeal Filing Fees: LKR 10,000 to 50,000 | Appeal Legal Fees: LKR 200,000 to 1,000,000+]
Execution of the Court Order (If the defendant refuses to comply, the court enforces the ruling through eviction orders, police assistance, or compensation recovery.)

contractual_dispute_procedure.title: Step-by-Step Contractual Dispute Resolution Procedure in Sri Lanka
steps: Understanding the Contract Dispute (Identify the type of breach: non-payment, failure to perform, or violation of contract terms. Gather all necessary documents such as contracts, invoices, and communication records.)

Hiring a Commercial Lawyer (Consult a lawyer specializing in contract law to assess legal standing and possible solutions.) [Initial Consultation: LKR 10,000 to 50,000 | Case Preparation: LKR 50,000 to 250,000]
Sending a Legal Notice (The lawyer issues a formal demand to the defaulting party, requesting compliance within a set period, typically 7 to 30 days.) [Legal Notice Cost: LKR 5,000 to 20,000]

Negotiation and Settlement Attempts (Attempt resolution through direct discussions, mediation, or arbitration before filing a lawsuit.) [Mediation: LKR 5,000 to 25,000 | Arbitration: LKR 50,000 to 500,000+]

Filing a Lawsuit in the Appropriate Court (If no settlement is reached, the plaintiff files a case in either the District Court or Commercial High Court.) [District Court/Commercial High Court Filing Fees: LKR 3,000 to 20,000 | Stamp Duty: LKR 2,000 to 10,000]

Serving Summons to the Defendant (The court issues summons requiring the defendant to respond within 14 to 21 days. If they fail to appear, the court may proceed ex-parte.) [Summons Cost: LKR 1,500 to 5,000]

Court Hearings and Trial Process (Both parties present evidence, witnesses, and legal arguments. The case is reviewed by the judge and may take months to years.) [Legal Fees: LKR 100,000 to 500,000+ | Court Costs: LKR 5,000 to 20,000]

Court Judgment and Remedies (The court issues a decision, which may include enforcing the contract, awarding compensation, or terminating the contract.) [Appeal Costs (if applicable): LKR 10,000 to 50,000 | Lawyer Fees: LKR 200,000 tp 1,000,000+]

Execution of Court Order (If the defendant refuses to comply, the plaintiff can request enforcement through asset seizure, account freezing, or police intervention.) [Execution Cost: LKR 5,000 to 25,000]

medical_negligence_procedure.title: Step-by-Step Medical Negligence Claim Procedure in Sri Lanka
steps: Understanding Medical Negligence (Misdiagnosis, surgical errors, incorrect medication, lack of informed consent, failure to provide treatment.)

Consulting a Medical Malpractice Lawyer (Assess case strength, review medical records, estimate compensation.) [Initial Consultation: LKR 10,000 to 50,000 | Full Case Representation: LKR 100,000 to 500,000+]
Obtaining a Medical Expert Opinion (Independent medical professional reviews case, provides report as evidence.) [Expert Opinion Cost: LKR 50,000 to 200,000+]
Filing a Complaint with the Sri Lanka Medical Council (Optional) (SLMC reviews doctors conduct, may take disciplinary action.) [Filing Cost: Free | Legal Assistance: Additional fees apply]

Filing a Lawsuit in District Court or High Court (Claim compensation based on damages suffered.) [District Court (Under LKR 5M) | High Court (Over LKR 5M)] [Filing Fees: LKR 3,000 to 15,000 | Stamp Duty: LKR 1,000 to 5,000]
Serving Summons to the Defendant (Notifies doctor, hospital, or medical institution of lawsuit.) [Summons Cost: LKR 1,500 to 5,000]
Mediation and Settlement Discussions (Court may recommend mediation to resolve dispute without trial.) [Mediation: Usually free]
Trial Proceedings in Court (Both parties present evidence, witnesses, and expert opinions.) [Legal Fees: LKR 250,000 to 1,500,000+]
Court Judgment and Compensation Award (Court decides based on medical evidence and negligence claim.) [Court Costs: LKR 5,000 to 25,000 | Compensation varies based on damages]
Appeals Process (If necessary) (Appeal to Court of Appeal or Supreme Court if unsatisfied with ruling.) [Appeal Costs: LKR 200,000 to 1,000,000+]

defamation_procedure.title: Step-by-Step Defamation Case Procedure in Sri Lanka
steps: Understanding Defamation (Defamation is categorized as libel (written) or slander (spoken). Plaintiffs must prove reputational harm and malicious intent.)
Hiring a Lawyer (Consult a defamation lawyer to assess case strength and gather evidence.) [Consultation Fees: LKR 10,000 to 50,000 | Full Representation: LKR 100,000 to 500,000+]
Sending a Legal Notice (Lawyer issues a formal demand for retraction, apology, or compensation before litigation.) [Legal Notice Cost: LKR 10,000 to 30,000]

Filing a Case in Court (Civil cases are filed in the District Court for monetary damages, while criminal cases go to the Magistrates Court for penalties.) [Filing Fees: LKR 3,000 to 10,000 | Stamp Duty: LKR 1,000 to 5,000]
Serving Summons to the Defendant (The court issues a summons; if the defendant does not appear, the case may proceed ex-parte.) [Summons Cost: LKR 1,500 to5,000]

Court Hearings and Trial Proceedings (Both parties present evidence, including witness statements, publications, or recordings.) [Legal Fees: LKR 250,000 to 1,000,000+ | Court Fees: LKR 5,000 to 20,000]

Judgment and Compensation (If proven, the plaintiff may be awarded damages or the defendant may face fines or imprisonment.) [Civil Compensation: LKR 500,000 to 10,000,000+ | Criminal Fines: LKR 50,000 to 500,000 | Imprisonment: Up to 2 years]
Appeals Process (If dissatisfied with the verdict, either party can appeal to the Court of Appeal or Supreme Court.) [Appeal Costs: LKR 300,000 to 1,000,000+]

assault_bodily_harm_procedure.title: Step-by-Step Procedure for Assault & Bodily Harm Cases in Sri Lanka
steps: Filing a Police Complaint (Report the incident at the nearest police station, providing details of the attack, assailant identity, and witnesses.) [Cost: Free]

Medical Examination & Report (Undergo medical examination at a government hospital or by a Judicial Medical Officer. The Medico-Legal Report will be used as evidence.) [Estimated Cost: LKR 1,500 to 5,000]

Police Investigation & Arrest (Police collect evidence, interview witnesses, and examine CCTV footage. If sufficient evidence is found, the suspect is arrested and presented before the Magistrates Court.) [Lawyer Consultation: LKR 10,000 to 50,000]
Filing Charges in the Magistrates Court (Police submit findings to the Magistrates Court, where the case is formally filed.) [Filing Fees: LKR 3,000 to 10,000]
Bail Hearing (If the accused is in custody, they may apply for bail. The court decides based on case severity.) [Bail Application: LKR 5,000 to 25,000 | Bail Amount: LKR 50,000 to 500,000+]

Trial & Evidence Presentation (Prosecution and defense present their arguments in the Magistrates Court, supported by medical reports, witness testimonies, and CCTV footage.) [Court Fees: LKR 5,000 to 15,000 | Legal Fees: LKR 100,000 to 500,000+]
Courts Decision & Sentencing (If found guilty, the accused may be fined, ordered to pay compensation, or sentenced to imprisonment.) [Appeal Costs (if applicable): LKR 200,000+]
Compensation & Civil Lawsuit (Victim may file a civil lawsuit in the District Court to claim medical expenses, loss of income, and emotional distress.) [Legal Fees: LKR 100,000 to 1,000,000+]
